Greater Geelong is Victoria's second city and it sits about 75 kilometres from Melbourne, an hour down the Princes Freeway. It has a genuine water frontage in the middle of town along Corio Bay and Eastern Beach, and behind that a stock of old wool stores and industrial buildings that have become raw event spaces. Those rooms are the reason many people choose Geelong, and they are also why event planners in Geelong spend more of a first meeting on infrastructure than on styling.

The region does not stop at the city. The Bellarine Peninsula runs east with cool climate vineyards around Drysdale and Portarlington and beaches at Ocean Grove and Barwon Heads, and there is a ferry across to Sorrento from Queenscliff. Geelong is also the gateway to the Great Ocean Road, so a share of local events are the opening night of a longer itinerary for guests staying on.

In and around Geelong

What are you planning in Geelong?

Six briefs make up most of the work here, and the first question on nearly all of them is the same: does the room come with anything, or are you bringing all of it in yourself.

Start with

Weddings

Two very different local shapes. A vineyard or beachside venue on the Bellarine that supplies most things, or a raw space near the waterfront that supplies four walls. The second is not cheaper once hire, catering, power and staff are added, but it does let you build the room you want.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Milestone birthdays and anniversaries here often land in a warehouse space or a club room rather than a restaurant, which is a good outcome if you like the look and a longer job than people expect. Truck access, a bump in window and a noise finish time are the three things to confirm early.

Find planners

Corporate events

Geelong carries manufacturing, health, insurance and university employers, and the local corporate calendar runs to conferences, awards nights, launches and staff days. A number of briefs come from Melbourne organisations wanting a change of scene an hour away, which puts accommodation and transport inside the quote.

Find planners

Engagement parties

Often on the Bellarine because the family has a connection there, and often in summer when the peninsula is full. Confirm the guest travel plan before the venue, since a party at Portarlington or Barwon Heads means a late drive back to Geelong or a room somewhere nearby.

Find planners

Proposals

Eastern Beach and the Corio Bay waterfront work in the middle of town, and the cliffs and beaches around Barwon Heads and Point Lonsdale work if you are prepared to drive. Check the wind off the bay, and remember Queenscliff and Sorrento are connected by ferry if the day is meant to continue.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Christenings, anniversaries, memorials and reunions are steady work, and a good share happen at home on the larger blocks through Highton, Newtown and Leopold. A marquee on a suburban lawn still needs power, a caterer's kitchen and somewhere for a delivery truck to stop.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Geelong?

The dividing line here is not the guest number, it is whether the venue is bare. A room that includes catering, staff and furniture can run on coordination. An empty wool store with a hired kitchen is a full planning job at any size.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Budget built and tracked
  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

Partial planning

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Often engaged four to eight months out.

  • Picks up from where you are
  • Fills the supplier gaps
  • Tidies the budget
  • Builds the run sheet
  • Hands back a plan you can follow

On-the-day coordination

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

  • Reads and stress-tests your plan
  • Confirms every supplier
  • Owns the run sheet
  • First point of contact on the day
  • Handles what goes sideways

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Geelong

The questions worth asking in Geelong are mostly about infrastructure and distance. These four separate planners who have built an event from nothing from planners who have only managed one.

No. 01

Ask what they have built in a raw space

An empty room needs power distribution, a kitchen the caterer can actually use, bathrooms at your guest number, furniture, lighting, staging and a bump in schedule. Ask for a specific event they have built in a bare venue, what it cost to service the space before anything decorative was ordered, and what they would do differently.

No. 02

Check the truck access and the bump in window

Old industrial buildings have doorways and laneways that were built for a different purpose. Ask where a truck loads, how far the gear travels from the door to the room, whether there is a lift, and how many hours you have before doors open. A four hour window and a long carry is a staffing question.

No. 03

Ask how they handle a Melbourne guest list

An hour on the freeway is close enough that guests will drive and far enough that they will not drive home after midnight. Ask how a planner usually solves it: room blocks in town, coaches back to Melbourne at a set time, or a start early enough that driving home is reasonable. All three work if decided early.

No. 04

Ask about the Bellarine specifically

The peninsula behaves differently from the city. Suppliers charge travel to get there, accommodation is holiday stock rather than hotel stock, and summer weekends are contested. Ask which Bellarine venues a planner has actually worked at, and whether their catering, hire and staffing quotes change once an event moves past Drysdale.

A bare room is the best value in Geelong and the most expensive mistake if nobody prices the services.

On the ground

Wool stores, the Bellarine and the freeway

Three things define event planning in this region: a stock of raw buildings near the water, a peninsula full of vineyards and beaches, and a freeway that puts Melbourne an hour away.

A raw room is a full build

The converted wool stores and industrial buildings near the Geelong waterfront are the region's signature spaces, and most of them arrive empty. That means a long hire list: tables, chairs, linen, glassware, a bar, a commercial kitchen or a catering tent, power distribution, lighting, heating in winter and bathrooms if the building's own are not sized for your numbers. None of that is a reason to avoid these rooms, which are why people choose Geelong in the first place. It is a reason to price the services before the styling, and to engage a planner who has done it.

The Bellarine is a separate market

Drive twenty minutes east of the city and the rules change. The Bellarine has cool climate vineyards around Drysdale and Portarlington, beach towns at Ocean Grove and Barwon Heads, and a ferry from Queenscliff across to Sorrento on the Mornington Peninsula. Venues there are more likely to include catering and less likely to be flexible about numbers or finish times. Suppliers add travel to reach them. Accommodation is holiday housing, which books by the week over summer, so a January event on the peninsula needs beds locked in before the guest list is settled.

An hour from Melbourne, and the road keeps going

Geelong sits at the junction of two guest flows: people coming down the Princes Freeway from Melbourne, and people heading on to the Great Ocean Road.

  • Expect a share of guests to make a weekend of it and plan accommodation accordingly
  • Melbourne suppliers will quote, usually with travel added, so compare against local ones
  • Freeway traffic on a Friday afternoon is heavier than the map suggests
  • If guests are continuing west, a Friday event leaves the weekend open for them

Questions

Planning an event in Geelong

How much does an event planner cost in Geelong?

The fee tracks the scope, and in this region the biggest variable is whether the venue is serviced or bare. A vineyard on the Bellarine that supplies catering, staff and furniture is a coordination job. A raw wool store where the planner is sourcing power, a kitchen, bathrooms, furniture and staffing is full planning work and will be quoted as such. Ask for a fee against the specific venue rather than a starting price.

What does an empty venue actually add to the budget?

More than most people allow, and it is worth listing before you fall in love with a room. Power distribution, a catering kitchen or tent, bathrooms sized for your guest number, tables, chairs, linen, glassware, a bar, lighting, heating for winter, and the labour to install and remove all of it. Ask a planner for that list priced against your numbers, then compare the total with a serviced venue before deciding.

Will Melbourne suppliers travel to Geelong?

Most will, and the freeway makes it straightforward, but travel usually appears on the quote and it compounds when a supplier is needed for a delivery, a setup and a collection. Geelong has its own base of caterers, hire companies, florists and entertainers, so get local quotes alongside the Melbourne ones. Where a Melbourne supplier is worth the travel, ask whether the fee covers a single trip or every visit.

Is the Bellarine harder to plan than the city?

Not harder, but different. Venues around Drysdale, Portarlington, Ocean Grove and Barwon Heads sit further from suppliers, so delivery windows are tighter and travel charges apply. Accommodation is holiday stock that fills over summer and long weekends. The ferry between Queenscliff and Sorrento is useful if part of your guest list is coming from the Mornington Peninsula, and it is worth checking timetables before you set a start time.

Do many guests turn a Geelong event into a weekend?

A good share do, because the city sits at the start of the Great Ocean Road. That is an advantage worth using rather than ignoring. Give guests a short note on what is nearby, hold accommodation early for summer dates, and consider a Friday event so people have the weekend to travel on. It also softens the late night driving problem for anyone who would otherwise head back to Melbourne.

How far ahead should we book?

Twelve months for a Saturday between November and March, and longer for one of the small number of raw spaces near the waterfront that people come specifically to use. Coordination only can be arranged four to eight weeks out, but the venue and the caterer close first. If your date lands in January on the Bellarine, treat accommodation as the first booking rather than the last one.
